solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pluck shown in American kidnapping

definitions.meaning: to pluck is to grab or pull something away quickly
in US slang a kidnapping or abduction is called by this word

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a quick grab, and American criminal slang for an abduction.

clue.text: Room with a view?

definitions.meaning: room means space, range or latitude to act
the word ends instruments for viewing, such as tele- and micro- versions

explanation.definitionFit: It means range or latitude, and is also the viewing-instrument suffix used alone.

clue.text: They draw back before going for gold

definitions.text: They draw back before going for gold

parts.words: They draw back before going for gold
parts.note: bowmen draw the bowstring back before aiming at the gold bullseye of the target

explanation.definitionFit: Bowmen pull the string back and aim for the gold centre ring of an archery target.

clue.text: Purge has racist components

indicators.note: the parts of the words are taken apart and rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone claims a purge has racist elements in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'components' signals that HAS and RACIST are broken up and reassembled.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotional cleansing or release is a purging of feeling, so the noun matches.

clue.text: Girl from near Wigan — a sixfooter

indicators.note: the letters are taken out from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A very tall girl comes from somewhere near Wigan, a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'near Wigan'. The six feet are an insect's legs, not height; Wigan is a town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect has six legs, so it is jokingly a creature with six feet.

clue.text: Expert clad in an item of protective clothing

indicators.note: something clad in another is wrapped by it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: taken as written
a pro is an expert or professional

explanation.surface: A skilled worker wears a piece of safety gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore-like garment tied at the front protects clothes while cooking or working.

clue.text: Nick has a favourite dog

parts.note: to nick is to steal, and so is to whip in British slang
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick owns a favourite dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a man's name but is the verb meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender racing breed of greyhound type, so an example of the general term.

clue.text: Favours seeing only high-class acts

parts.note: good means of high quality or class
turns are acts on a variety bill

explanation.surface: A theatre manager books only top-quality acts as a favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind helpful deeds done for someone are favours, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: He earned a name for exclusive treatment in Ireland

definitions.text: He earned a name for exclusive treatment in Ireland

parts.words: He earned a name for exclusive treatment in Ireland
parts.note: the Irish land agent Captain Charles ... was shunned by tenants in 1880, giving the language a word for ostracism

explanation.walkthrough: Captain Charles Boycott, an English land agent in County Mayo, was ostracised by locals in 1880 and his surname became the word for such shunning.
explanation.definitionFit: The agent's surname became the common word for collectively refusing to deal with someone.

clue.text: He may be prepared to sell his land

definitions.text: He may be prepared to sell his land

parts.words: He may be prepared to sell his land
parts.note: selling out one's country, not real estate, marks a betrayer

explanation.definitionFit: A betrayer of his nation sells out his own country to its enemies.

clue.text: About to become involved in quarrel — shame!

indicators.note: one piece becoming involved in another goes inside it

parts.note: a dispute is a quarrel
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is about to be drawn into a quarrel and feels ashamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but the two words split: 'About' is one piece and 'to become involved in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in bad repute or disgrace is a state of shame, a close synonym.

clue.text: No relative may make such a telling statement

indicators.note: the words may be made into something else by rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A remark so striking that no relative could have said it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may make' tells you to rearrange NO RELATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprising disclosure is a statement that tells something previously unknown.

clue.text: Irishman hot on the trail

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is a stock Irish name in crosswords
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An Irishman is in hot pursuit of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot on the trail' reads as one phrase, but 'on' places H after PAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail and a track or way are synonyms for a route to follow.

clue.text: What pacifists have but don't use

definitions.text: What pacifists have but don't use

indicators.note: the word pacifists has a shorter word contained within its letters

explanation.surface: Peace lovers possess the means of violence but never employ them.
explanation.definitionFit: Clenched hands for punching are what a peace lover owns but would never use.

clue.text: Treacherous outlaw in fiction

parts.note: false means disloyal or treacherous
Robin Hood is the outlaw of English legend

explanation.surface: A treacherous outlaw appears in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fiction' looks like the outlaw's setting, but 'fiction' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An untruth or lie is a fiction in the sense of something made up.

clue.text: Bird seen in a colourful spring

parts.note: red is a colour, so colourful here gives the shade
a start is a sudden jump or spring

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted during a bright, colourful springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but here it is a startled jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird of the thrush family with a rust-coloured tail.

clue.text: Late payment?

parts.note: late means dead, so this is tax paid on the estate of someone who has died

explanation.definitionFit: Tax levied on a dead person's estate is literally a payment for the late.

clue.text: Gets angry when signs of distress are seen?

definitions.text: when signs of distress are seen?
definitions.meaning: distress rockets sent into the sky are literally aloft

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means loses one's temper, and distress rockets that have gone aloft literally fit.

clue.text: Ruth Rendell's first English detective

indicators.note: the first letter of the novelist's surname is taken

parts.note: Inspector Morse is Colin Dexter's Oxford detective

explanation.surface: A crime fan names the first English detective created by novelist Ruth Rendell.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth looks like the novelist's first name, but it is an old word for pity or regret. Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an archaic word for sorrow or regret, as in ruthless meaning without pity.

clue.text: Helps beast in distress

indicators.note: letters in distress are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone comes to the aid of an animal in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' tells you to rearrange BEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist or encourage someone is to help them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Feeling I'm one to get pushed around

indicators.note: letters that get pushed around are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains of a sense of being bullied by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get pushed around' rearranges the letters of I'M ONE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong feeling such as joy or anger is a sentiment, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Wide smile gives support

definitions.meaning: to smile broadly or a broad grin
a horizontal timber or girder that holds up a structure

explanation.surface: A broad grin can be a source of encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad grin and a load-bearing timber share the same word.

clue.text: Decisive moment in game as striker takes position on the field

parts.note: a match is struck to light it
point is a fielding position in cricket

explanation.surface: A footballer moves into position on the pitch at the decisive moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer but is a match you strike. Point is a fielding position in cricket, close to the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the point that can decide the whole contest is the deciding moment.

clue.text: Fashion prototype

definitions.meaning: to fashion is to shape or form something
a first version or pattern from which copies are made

explanation.definitionFit: To shape something and a pattern to copy from are both senses of the word.

clue.text: The fall that followed Eve

parts.note: eve means evening, and darkness falls after it

explanation.definitionFit: After evening comes the time of darkness, as in the phrase nightfall.

clue.text: Rust found in the central shaft

indicators.note: one piece found in another sits inside it

parts.note: the core is the central part
a rod is a shaft or pole

explanation.surface: Rust is discovered on the main axle of a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central shaft' reads as one machine part, but the adjective and noun are separate pieces, one wrapping the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To rust is to eat away metal by oxidation, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Excursions from Tunis go free

indicators.note: letters set free are loose to rearrange

explanation.surface: Trips from the Tunisian capital cost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like no charge, but signals rearranging TUNIS GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Excursions and trips out are synonyms for short pleasure journeys.

clue.text: Lives well in the outskirts of Dallas

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other
the outside letters of the city name are used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lives comfortably in suburban Dallas.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live there, a formal synonym.

clue.text: The sound of a seal or swan

indicators.note: the sound of a word means one that is spoken the same way

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a signet ring

explanation.surface: Someone asks what noise a seal or swan makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sound of' looks like an animal noise but means a word that sounds like another.
explanation.definitionFit: A young swan is called this, so the clue's bird is fair as the general class.
